statement: Let $f(x)=\dfrac{2x}{x^{2}+1}$. Find the range of $f$ and the coordinates of its stationary points.
solution: $f'(x)=\dfrac{2(1-x^{2})}{(x^{2}+1)^{2}}$, which vanishes at $x=\pm1$. We have $f(1)=1$ and $f(-1)=-1$. As $x\to\pm\infty$, $f(x)\to0$, so $f$ increases to a maximum of $1$ at $x=1$ and decreases to a minimum of $-1$ at $x=-1$; the range is $[-1,1]$.
hints: Examine the limiting behaviour as $x	o\pm\infty$.
